selectionPriority: All required lessons selected; enabled questions only; correct review mode.
Whole questions, no duplicate IDs or two variants from the same family.
Reach exactly 20 marks when possible; otherwise use the largest attainable total below 20 and announce it before starting. Never split a question to fill the budget.
Among sets at that total, minimise the absolute difference between recall fraction and 0.5.
Prefer less-seen questions as a tie-break, then seeded random order.
shortPoolMessage: Only {marks} marks are available from these lessons. Start this shorter session or select more lessons.
timeClaim: Marks standardise workload approximately, not elapsed time. Do not promise an exact duration or run a compulsory timer.

eligibility.blockedQuestionAction: List missing lesson titles; let the student select them explicitly.
eligibility.futureTopicAction: Forces and Electricity shown only as planned, with no selectable question pool.

marking.submission: Check the whole question once; warn about empty parts and allow an intentional partial submission.
marking.choice: One selected option per part. Mark by stable option ID, never its displayed letter. Record shuffled order with the draft.
marking.numeric: Accept finite decimal, grouped thousands, decimal comma, and scientific-notation equivalents within authored tolerance. Units shown or explicitly selected; convert only units allowed by that part. No eval.
marking.ecf: Evaluate only authored later-step rules after an upstream attempted numeric error. Blank, non-finite, impossible or invalid-domain values cannot seed ECF. A correct response earns direct credit first. Each mark is awarded once.
marking.ecfFeedback: Show Direct marks and Method marks (error carried forward), plus the original error and the later correct operation on the student’s value.
marking.write: One open response test. Student writes first, reveals bullet marking points, then enters a whole-number score from 0 to the maximum in a labelled box. No automatic prose grading.
marking.scoreSeparation: Keep direct, ECF and self-assessed marks separate in records and summaries. Hints, reveal and retries are separate events; retain first submission.

language.question: Use appropriate Pearson command words and exam-like sentences: State, Identify, Calculate, Determine, Compare, Explain, Suggest. Do not label a task Evaluate if it asks only for a description.
language.feedback: Use short, natural student-facing English. Give the correction, then explain the selected misconception. Avoid simply saying incorrect.
language.completion: An opening answer sentence may be supplied. Only the selected missing points earn marks. Each gap has a clear purpose and all choices fit its grammar.

preserve: Dark navy desktop sidebar; Practice, Mistakes and Progress navigation.
White workspace, serif headings and sans-serif instructions/controls.
Green actions and dark pink/red Finish session control.
Dark mobile session bar and existing setup/session distinction.
Prominent complete task instructions; generous diagrams with accessible enlarge control.
Optional celebrations, sound preference and reduced-motion support.
necessaryChanges: Group selectable lessons under Waves, Forces and Electricity. Keep selected checkboxes when closing a group.
Show actual marks in setup/session summary; retain question position as secondary navigation.
Add calculation boxes, completion controls and a single self-score field to existing answer area.
Display ECF method credit with text, not colour alone.
Show missing prerequisites and shorter-pool totals adjacent to Start.
askBefore: Changing navigation destinations, palette, page hierarchy or normal session workflow.
Replacing current phone controls with a new interaction pattern.
Adding accounts, cloud progress, compulsory timers or teacher dashboards.
ui.storage: Use AAQ-specific progress/preference/session keys, separate from the OCR app. Stable question IDs plus contentVersion; changing marking semantics creates a new compatible version or migration. Never clear unrelated localStorage.

release.referenceCore: Pure selection, numeric/choice marking and self-score validation supplied and tested. It is a reference module, not a completed browser interface.
release.studentGate: Do not present unreviewed material as teacher-approved. A teacher preview mode can load draft questions.
